name: Yin Fengshan
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Fengshan Group Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603810)
profile: Yin Fengshan (b. 1947) built Jiangsu Fengshan Group, a pesticide and agrochemical maker in Dafeng, Yancheng, from a county agrochemical plant he ran from 1988 into a Shanghai-listed company. He remains chairman and controlling shareholder; his daughter Yin Ping (co-listed on Hurun) is president and vice chair.
interesting_fact: Fengshan's predecessor was Dafeng County Agrochemical Plant No. 2, which Yin ran as factory director from 1988-1993 before restructuring it into Yancheng Fengshan Pesticide Co. and later a listed group.
deep_cut_fact: Before pesticides, Yin was deputy director of the Changcheng Electrical Equipment Factory in Caomiao Township, Dafeng County (1986-88); he is also a vice president of the China Pesticide Industry Association.
notes: Still chairing board meetings in 2025 per SSE filing (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-04-29/1223386457.PDF). Bio source is user-submitted (maigoo); cross-check with prospectus. Best route: company board secretary via SSE disclosures.

name: Joseph V. Topper Jr.
current_role: Chairman, CrossAmerica Partners LP (NYSE: CAPL); CEO, Dunne Manning Holdings (Topper Group); director, CoastalSouth Bancshares
profile: Allentown, PA fuel-distribution entrepreneur who bought his family's retail fuel business in 1987 and founded what became Lehigh Gas Corp., later taken public as Lehigh Gas Partners/CrossAmerica Partners. He was CAPL's CEO 2012-15, retook control via the Topper Group in 2019 and is chairman; he also runs the Dunne Manning real-estate/investing group.
interesting_fact: A 1977 Villanova accounting graduate (and former CPA), he chaired Villanova University's Board of Trustees from 2017 to 2020 after serving as trustee since 2010.
deep_cut_fact: His fuel empire started with his family's gas business on MacArthur Road in Whitehall Township, PA, which he bought in 1987; five years later he started the company that became Lehigh Gas Corp. (now Dunne Manning Inc.).
notes: Energy/fuel-retail angle fits the podcast. Bio lists him on board of Patriot Acquisition Corp. since March 2026. Corporate main line published on CAPL site (610-625-8000, Allentown HQ).

name: Geoffrey Kent
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Abercrombie & Kent (luxury travel group)
profile: Born in 1942 while his parents were on safari in what is now Zambia and raised in Kenya, Kent co-founded Abercrombie & Kent with his parents in 1962 while still in the British Army, pioneering the photographic (not hunting) luxury safari. He grew it into a global luxury and expedition travel group and, now in his 80s, still personally hosts A&K's flagship private-jet journeys (2026, 2027).
interesting_fact: He pioneered private-jet luxury touring with 'The Royal Air Tour' in 1989 using Concorde with British Airways, and as a polo player captained teams that won the US Open and played alongside King Charles III.
deep_cut_fact: At 16, after being expelled from school, he made a solo ~5,000-mile, two-month motorbike ride from Nairobi to Cape Town, credited as the first by motorcycle; he recounts it in his 2015 memoir 'Safari: A Memoir of a Worldwide Travel Pioneer'.

public_contacts.value: JFawcett@abercrombiekent.com (Jean Fawcett, Senior Manager Media Relations, USA)

notes: Very media-friendly founder (memoirs, TV series, hosts trips). Also Honorary Consul of Kenya to Monaco. Best route: A&K global comms.

name: William Asprey
current_role: Founder, William & Son (Mayfair luxury jeweller, gunmaker and outfitter)
profile: A seventh-generation member of the Asprey dynasty (Asprey, the Bond Street luxury house founded 1781 by his ancestor of the same name), William Asprey founded William & Son in Mayfair in 1999. The business sells fine jewellery, timepieces, leather and homeware plus a gun room and field sports range, largely made by British craftsmen, and holds a Royal Warrant.
interesting_fact: His ancestor William Asprey founded Asprey in 1781 as a silk-printing business in Mitcham, Surrey; the family sold the group to Prince Jefri Bolkiah's Amedeo in 1995 for GBP244m.
deep_cut_fact: William & Son was set up in 1999 by William Asprey as the seventh generation of the family, with a stated mission of keeping traditional British crafts alive by working with artisans and designer-makers.
notes: Current status/involvement in William & Son not re-verified (web search budget exhausted). Not an energy/tech figure; luxury retail angle.

name: David R Little
current_role: Chairman and CEO, DXP Enterprises Inc. (NASDAQ: DXPE), Houston
profile: David Little has led the Houston industrial distributor DXP Enterprises (pumps, bearings, power transmission, MRO and supply-chain services, with heavy oil & gas exposure) since 1983, when he became president and CEO of its predecessor SEPCO. He drove a merger and acquisition strategy, took the company public in 1996 as DXP, and remains chairman and CEO per SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: DXP traces back to 1908, when Charles A. Levins founded Southern Engine and Pump Company in Houston to sell pumps to farmers; the business became SEPCO in 1979 and DXP at its 1996 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Founder-family heir George N. Allen (grandson of the 1908 founder) personally chose Little as his successor in 1983; Little then merged SEPCO with Shoreline Supply to make it the largest pump distributor in North America.
notes: Strong energy (oil & gas pumps/industrial supply) angle. No press email found on site; IR contact via SEC filings/press releases (ir.dxpe.com blocked to automated fetch).
